name: Losing Loadum
description: Losing Loadum (or Losing Lodam) is an intriguing ancestor of the Hearts family, dating back to 16th-century England. It is a 'penalty trick' game where the objective is to avoid winning specific high-value cards called 'Loaders'. The game is unique for its elimination mechanic: any player reaching 31 points is immediately 'out'. It also features a rare 'hidden trump' system where trumps are determined only when a player first fails to follow suit.

content.text: Losing Loadum (or Losing Lodam) is an intriguing ancestor of the Hearts family, dating back to 16th-century England. It is a 'penalty trick' game where the objective is to avoid winning specific high-value cards called 'Loaders'. The game is unique for its elimination mechanic: any player reaching 31 points is immediately 'out'. It also features a rare 'hidden trump' system where trumps are determined only when a player first fails to follow suit.
First mentioned in 1591. It was a favorite of the Elizabethan and Stuart courts before being simplified into modern Hearts and Black Maria.
Standard 52-card deck. Ranked Ace (high) down to 2.
Cards are dealt evenly. A small 'talon' of remaining cards is placed face-down.

items.text: Great Loadum: The standard version without the 31-point elimination.
Hearts: The modern global avoidance game.
